title: EPIC: Qualified Ball Landing, Bounce, Roll, and Ground-Surface Modeling
body:
## Status as of 2026-09-19

Status as of 2026-09-19
- Done: versioned ground contracts + strict JSON; 3D impulse/bounce; skid-to-roll with slopes/regions (#4271); sourced profiles, persistence, migration, Upstream terrain adapter (#4272); total-distance metrics, target projection, seeded regional variation (#4273); PyQt ground playback tab incl. GroundPlayback3DView + React playback/comparison/persistence (#4274); qualified execution job + loopback Python authority + browser client (#4369); Python/Rust conformance corpus (#4321, #5189).
- Open: UpstreamDrift exact-pin adapters and clean-install smoke (#4276, cross-repo); calibration evidence for surface presets (defaults still illustrative); matched-client visual/a11y evidence for the ground surfaces.
- Children #4268-#4270, #4275 already closed.

---

## Objective

Create a qualified, versioned post-landing physics system for golf-ball first contact, repeated bounce, skid, pure roll, slope and regional surface transitions so the flight workbench can report total distance without ever mislabeling carry. The reusable contracts/kernel live in Tools; UpstreamDrift consumes an exact reviewed Tools revision through thin adapters.

Parent campaign: #4135
Related flight epic: #4191
Related metric contract: #4194
Related variation: #4142 and #4144
Related 3D playback: #4200
Related release gate: #4201
Cross-application parity: #4260

## Audited reuse map

### Adopt from Tools

- Preserve the existing explicit `GroundModelResult` boundary and stable total-distance, roll-distance, bounce-count, and final-offline metric IDs. These remain unavailable unless a qualified ground result is supplied.
- Reuse validated putting-scale stimp, skid-transition, pure-roll stopping, slope, deterministic variation, strict serialization, provenance, cancellation, typed termination, and energy-accounting patterns where their assumptions apply.
- Do not reuse the complete putting workflow as a high-speed landing solver.

### Adapt from UpstreamDrift

- Adapt the split terrain/material package through a narrow one-way adapter: friction, rolling resistance, restitution, hardness, grass height, compressibility/damping, moisture, elevation, regions, downhill direction, and surface normals.
- Treat putting-green rolling and Rust contact code as reviewed reference algorithms/API shapes, not qualified implementations.
- Do not extend the duplicate legacy terrain representation or import UpstreamDrift domain classes into the Tools kernel.

## Scientific boundaries

- Current airborne trajectories terminate at a relative launch plane and do not preserve terminal angular velocity; both must be corrected before ground physics is trustworthy.
- Carry is first physical ground contact. Total distance is available only from this qualified model.
- Tee height, launch elevation, ball radius, terrain elevation, and surface normal must affect physical contact once and must never be double-counted.
- Default surface values are illustrative until calibration evidence, sources, uncertainty, and applicability are recorded.
- The current Upstream scalar landing helper and Rust `(1-friction)` tangential law are not acceptable production laws.
- The React client must consume the same qualified kernel/contract; do not create another independent TypeScript physics port.

## Acceptance criteria

### Contracts and transfer state

- [ ] Versioned strict contracts define ground surface profiles, contact state, phases, trajectory points, request/result, event ledger, termination, warnings, calibration status, and provenance.
- [ ] Canonical frame is explicit (`x` downrange, `y` up, `z` right); all Upstream terrain/frame adapters are versioned and tested.
- [ ] Flight-to-ground transfer preserves physical time, center position, linear velocity, full angular-velocity vector, ball mass/radius/inertia, terrain elevation, and surface normal.
- [ ] The richer result adapts backward-compatibly to the existing compact `GroundModelResult`.

### Physics

- [ ] A validated 3D normal/tangential impulse law supports restitution, Coulomb/sticking friction, sphere inertia, full spin coupling, arbitrary normals, passive energy checks, and outgoing/grazing-state rejection.
- [ ] Deterministic repeated bounce transitions to skid, pure roll, regional surface changes, slopes, and final stop with typed cancellation/out-of-bounds/step-limit/numerical states.
- [ ] Low-speed limiting cases agree with analytic skid/roll references and documented time-step convergence bounds.

### Surfaces, results, and studies

- [ ] Users can edit sourced, unit-explicit ground parameters with finite bounds, calibration status, provenance, and clear illustrative warnings.
- [ ] Fairway, rough, green, fringe, bunker, tee, and hard-surface presets exist only where validated; unsupported combinations remain explicit.
- [ ] Results include carry, bounce distance, skid distance, roll distance, total distance, final position/offline, bounce count, ground time, model ID/version, surface ID/version, warnings, and termination.
- [ ] Ground variables participate in seeded variation, dispersion, target-hold, optimization, and wind/strategy workflows without fabricating results for misses or failures.

### Matched clients and integration

- [ ] PyQt6 and React expose the same applicable parameters/results and show distinct airborne, bounce, skid, and roll phases in synchronized 3D playback and exports.
- [ ] Carry and total markers, active assumptions, comparison overlays, scrub/play/pause/restart/loop, camera interaction, and accessible tables are verified.
- [ ] UpstreamDrift API/PyQt/React consumers use an exact Tools pin and thin adapters; feature-parity manifests and both handoffs are current.

### Verification

- [ ] RED-first analytic, property, golden, frame-invariance, persistence, failure-state, Python/Rust/WASM parity, UI interaction, visual, accessibility, performance, and scientific-validation tests pass.
- [ ] Protected checks pass on exact reviewed commits; queued/skipped/zero-job contexts are not accepted as passing.

## Planned child workstreams

- [ ] Versioned surface/contact/trajectory/result/provenance contracts
- [ ] Correct physical flight-to-ground geometry and terminal spin
- [ ] Validated 3D contact impulse and repeated bounce
- [ ] Skid-to-roll dynamics on slopes and regional surfaces
- [ ] Sourced profiles, persistence, calibration, and Upstream terrain adapters
- [ ] Total-distance metrics, target/solver/variation integration
- [ ] Matched PyQt6/React controls and 3D playback
- [ ] Python/Rust/WASM parity, validation, and performance
- [ ] UpstreamDrift exact-pin integration and protected release

## Engineering rules

Use RED -> GREEN -> REFACTOR TDD, Design by Contract at every unit/frame/schema boundary, DRY canonical physics and transformations, and Law of Demeter facades. Reject NaN/Inf, invalid ranges, unsupported schemas, frame ambiguity, silent unit conversion, energy creation, and unqualified defaults. Preserve typed miss/no-ground/cancel/failure outcomes.

## Definition of done

Close only after every child is merged through protected review; carry and total distance remain scientifically distinct; exact cross-runtime fixtures, client UI evidence, persistence migrations, performance, surface provenance, clean-install integration, handoffs, and known limitations are linked in a final evidence comment.



## Tracked child issues

- #4268 — landing, surface, bounce, roll, and result contracts
- #4269 — flight-to-ground geometry and terminal-spin continuity
- #4270 — 3D impulse response and repeated bounce
- #4271 — skid-to-roll transition, slope, and surface regions
- #4272 — ground profiles, persistence, calibration, and terrain adapters
- #4273 — total-distance metrics, targets, solver, and variation support
- #4274 — matched PyQt/React controls and 3D playback
- #4275 — Python/Rust/WASM conformance, validation, and performance
- #4276 — UpstreamDrift exact-pin integration and release verification

Cross-surface parity is tracked in #4260.

## Folded in from backlog triage 2026-09-19

- [ ] UpstreamDrift: repin to the reviewed Tools revision, add thin API/PyQt/React ground adapters, update parity manifests and both handoffs (#4276) (from #4276)
